summary: Norway House Airport (YNE/CYNE) is a small regional airport serving the Cree Nation community of Norway House, located on the northern shore of Lake Winnipeg in Manitoba, Canada. It functions as a vital transportation link for this remote community, supporting both passenger travel and the supply of essential goods. The airport plays an important role in connecting northern Manitoba to Winnipeg and other regional destinations.
faqs:
Q: What is the airport code for Norway House Airport?
A: The IATA code is YNE and the ICAO code is CYNE.

Q: Where is Norway House Airport located?
A: It is located in Norway House, Manitoba, Canada, on the northern shore of Lake Winnipeg, approximately 450 km north of Winnipeg.

Q: What airlines serve Norway House Airport?
A: The airport is primarily served by regional carriers offering flights to and from Winnipeg, with scheduled service typically operated by smaller turboprop aircraft.

Q: Is Norway House Airport open year-round?
A: Yes, the airport operates year-round, though winter weather conditions can occasionally affect flight schedules in this northern Manitoba region.
transport_tips: The airport is located a short drive from the Norway House community centre, and ground transportation options are limited, so arranging a pickup in advance is recommended. Taxis and shuttle services may be available but should be booked ahead due to the small size of the community. Travelers connecting to Winnipeg should note that flight schedules are limited, typically with only one or two flights per day.
local_tip: If you have a wait at the airport, take a short trip into Norway House to visit the historic Mission Church, one of the oldest stone churches in Western Canada, and explore the local heritage center showcasing Cree culture and the area's fur trade history.
